newsitem.title: UK: British Midland says UK-Ireland top cargo routes.
newsitem.headline: British Midland says UK-Ireland top cargo routes.

text.p: British Midland has identified London Heathrow-Belfast as its top revenue-earning cargo route, followed by Heathrow-Dublin, cargo manager Terry Greetham told Reuters in an interview.
Both are operated by a combination of Boeing 737-300 and -400 passenger aircraft, which can uplift up to three tonnes of cargo per flight.

After Belfast and Dublin, Greetham listed the following core ex-Heathrow routes in order of revenue-earning importance to British Midland: Glasgow, Brussels, Edinburgh, Amsterdam, Paris, Frankfurt, Palma, Leeds, Nice, Zurich, Bergen, Orly, Teesside and Prague.
Brussels and Amsterdam were the carrier's key Continental Europe cargo destinations because they acted as express hubs for a number of integrators and other distribution companies.
"These days we are placing a lot of emphasis on the express end of the market," he said

The airline starts twice-daily 737-300 services from Heathrow to another major European express hub, Cologne/Bonn, from May 26. One flight will continue on from Cologne/Bonn to Rome, and will be the first time British Midland has operated a "fifth freedom" service, between two countries other than its home base.
British Midland has a passenger code-sharing agreement with Lufthansa for the new UK-Germany-Italy flights and Greetham said he had talked with the German carrier about cargo sales co-operation.
But he said British Midland would also soon appoint a cargo general sales agent in Germany.
Greetham said the Prague service was launched in October 1995 on a daily, not a twice-daily basis as he would have liked.
"But it is an interesting route. We started it from scratch and believe there is demand to be tapped," he said.

British Midland said it was too early to forecasat earnings from Heathrow to Copenhagen, Gothenburg and Oslo, started on April 21. British Midland is 40 percent owned by SAS - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706; fax +5017
